I have a CCW permit and have rarely used it so my answer is yes for a few reasons (I'm speaking about my state laws, yours may differ).

  • If you want to transport a few pistols (in their own cases) the logical choice is to put them all into one bag, technically this is concealed carry.

  • You can inadvertently conceal carry when open carrying. For example your jacket or shirt briefly conceals your firearm. No idea what an LEO would do in a situation like this, but better safe than sorry.

  • If I recall correctly placing a firearm in the console/glovebox of your car is considered concealed carry. If you ever want to take a road trip in state (or through other states with CCW reciprocity) it allows you to have a firearm within reach if needed.

  • Like the outdoors and want some extra protection? You can now have a firearm in your backpack if you want, above also related.

  • I'm no longer required to pass or pay for any background check when purchasing a firearm. Disclaimer I can't say this will be the same for your state.

  • You'll learn, or get a refresher course, in some basic firearm safety and very basic shooting skills. I would still recommend additional classes if you're not comfortable carrying though.

  • You'll now have the option to conceal carry if you want to. Key word here being want. A CCW is in no way an obligation to conceal carry.

  • You'll learn about your local self defense laws and when it is appropriate in the eyes of the law to use deadly force.

  • They'll drill into your head, and rightfully so, that you are under no obligation to use your firearm in an emergency.

The last two are big one for me lately since the media seems to think that all gun owners are somehow out looking for confrontation. Since you're considering getting a CCW you probably already know that this couldn't be further from the truth, but knowing when to use a weapon is extremely important. We don't need any more incidents like this.

Like I said in the before I almost never use mine, but I'm glad I got it. If you have the money and time to spare I would highly recommend it, I doubt you'll regret it.
